text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to #incidents, @maya, @kira, @mike — GPU queue depth in us-east-1-prod exceeded emergency threshold (queue > 95th percentile cap). Autoscaler reports repeated scale-out failures. Paging SRE + runtime.

maya: On it. jumping in — are we seeing errors or just backlog? can someone paste the autoscaler logs?

kira: early quick triage: we are seeing repeated CUDA Xid entries from the node driver combined with OOMs in the runtime container. that reduces effective GPU capacity — autoscaler tried to add replicas but new pods hit node-level eviction/driver failures.

kira: sample from node kernel logs:
```
[2026-06-12T14:02:57Z] NVRM: Xid (71: Il) 79c3c4a0 00000000 00000000
[2026-06-12T14:02:58Z] kernel: Device driver forced reset on GPU 0
[2026-06-12T14:03:01Z] kubelet: Pod runtime terminated with OOMKilled, container=runner
```

mike: autoscaler events (snippet):
```
2026-06-12T14:03:05Z scale_request: desired=40 current=32 reason=queue_growth
2026-06-12T14:03:07Z scale_result: failed reason=node-sched-evict-limit; nodes_available=0
2026-06-12T14:03:09Z scale_result: suppressed reason=quota_soft_limit reached for pool=prod-gpu-us-east
```

jess: so two problems stacking: (1) driver/runtime instability taking GPUs out of rotation -> reduces headroom, (2) autoscaler hitting pool soft limit / hit quota so even when nodes are healthy we can't scale. we need short-term capacity and a mitigation for driver instability.

alex: customer impact: latency spike + 502s for some generation paths. alerting query shows ~12% of requests in us-east saw token-delay > 2s and 1.8% returned errors between 14:02–14:12. noisy for high-volume customers; CS is getting tickets.

olivia: pinging support and PMs — sending initial impact note to customers with mitigation ETA.

kira: quick plan proposal:
- mark affected nodes cordoned to prevent new pods
- drain the worst-off nodes with graceful eviction to surface logs
- temporarily raise pool soft limit (manual override) + request emergency capacity add (+4 nodes) while we stabilize
- rollback last driver rollout to previous known-good image (tag: driver-v1.14 -> v1.13)
- restart runtime pods on healthy nodes

mike: I can do manual capacity add to dedicated pool, but will need approval from infra lead. also can flip the autoscaler to aggressive cooldown to avoid oscillation once nodes come back.

maya: do we have a safe rollback procedure? last rollout started ~14:00, could be correlated.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-06-12T13:58 driver-v1.14 rollout in progress -> 40% nodes updated. rollout_job_id=drv-20260612-14

kira: yes — rollback path tested in staging. sequence:
1) pause driver rollout
2) set image to driver-v1.13 and restart kube-daemonset on affected ASG
3) monitor for Xid/OOM reduction for 2 minutes

jess: while that happens — we should also disable autoscaler soft-limit enforcement temporarily so the controller will accept scale-out; mike can add nodes to reserved capacity to avoid hitting quota.

mike: requesting manual pool increase +4 nodes now. doing: `infractl pool adjust --pool prod-gpu-us-east --delta 4 --reason \"emergency mitigation\"`

mike: update: command accepted, quota provider responding. expected node join 90–120s.

kira: rolling rollback now — performing: `kubectl set image daemonset/driver driver=image:driver-v1.13 --namespace=infra` and then `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/driver`.

kira: logs after restart (first 60s):
```
[2026-06-12T14:05:22Z] driver: init ok, firmware check passed
[2026-06-12T14:05:25Z] driver: health ping ok
```

maya: draining nodes with worst error rates now — draining node gpu-n-17 and gpu-n-18. using `kubectl drain gpu-n-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will move pods to new nodes once they join.

alex: CS note: initial mitigation underway; telling affected customers we expect reduced errors within 10–15m. will escalate to SEs for high-tier customers.

mike: new nodes are joining: 2/4 up at 14:06:43, 4/4 up at 14:07:55. autoscaler now sees capacity.

jess: I disabled the autoscaler soft-limit enforcement flag for the pool (flag: allow_overcommit=true) to allow immediate scaling. remember to re-enable after mitigation.

kira: after rollback and restarts, kernel Xid events dropping off. monitoring shows GPU availability increasing from 68% -> 94% over the next window.

kira: runtime pod OOMs also reduced once driver rolling restarted and bad nodes drained — looks correlated to driver v1.14 changes (investigating commit that increased pinned memory usage).

maya: customer impact update: error rate down to 0.6%, latency back to baseline for most customers at 14:12. CS pushing follow-ups.

olivia: sending customers the follow-up note: "We experienced a GPU capacity degradation due to a driver rollout resulting in OOM/Xid events that reduced available GPUs. We performed a rollback and added emergency capacity; service has been restored. Investigating root cause."

mike: making ticket to revert autoscaler soft flags and to clean up the emergency nodes after stabilization. will also open quota change request for pool if needed.

jess: next steps assigned: kira -> driver root cause (root cause candidate: v1.14 memory accounting change), mike -> infra + pool quota follow-up, maya -> incident ops writeup and postmortem, olivia -> customer comms and incident timeline.

alex: thanks team. posting initial summary + timeline to #postmortems once we stabilize.

maya: temporary status: mitigated at 14:12; monitoring for 30m. if metrics hold, we'll close page and start RCA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. pager cleared at 14:13. incident severity reduced to SEV3. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1768123456

maya: good work. add any follow-ups to the incident doc. I'll capture the logs and timeline.

kira: quick note — found one suspicious commit in v1.14: `gpu_memory_reserve` default bumped from 5% -> 12% which combined with pinned allocations triggered node OOMs under high packing. will include reproduction in postmortem.

mike: closing ops checklist items: nodes drained, driver rollback complete, emergency nodes will be removed in 2h if stable.

olivia: notifying customers the incident page is live and we'll follow up with RCA.

jess: thumbs up. handing back to oncall for monitoring — maya you own the watch window.

maya: owning watch window, thanks everyone. end of thread.
